title: proto_find_undecoded_data's marking loop is bounded by the field's extent and not by the bitmap's length, so a field reaching past the frame writes off the end
object: decoded, a packet-scope chunk of length/8 + 1 bytes
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the object is alive throughout. This is a SPATIAL row.
shape: `for (i = fi->start; i < fi->start + fi->length; i++) { decoded[i/8] |= 1 << (i%8); }` consults the FIELD extent only, so a field whose start plus length reaches past the frame drives the byte index past the bitmap
allocator_layer: wmem, a chunk the BLOCK or BLOCK_FAST allocator carved from a block g_malloc handed out. An inner allocator carved the crossed region, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row IS NESTED.
nested_why: an inner allocator (wmem) carved the crossed region out of a larger block it had itself obtained from g_malloc, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row IS NESTED.
fidelity: real allocator, model consumer. the frame is 64 bytes, so the bitmap is 9. The field claims start 56 and length 32, reaching index 87 and byte 10 -- past the bitmap and inside the block, both asserted.
live_proof: read from the PINNED source: v4.6.8:epan/proto.c contains the fix's `decoded_data_t` struct 4 times and the pre-fix bare `gchar* decoded = (gchar*)wmem_alloc0` 0 times. Two-sided. A fix-reversal.
distinguishing: the index here comes from the protocol tree's OWN field extents -- output of a sibling subsystem -- rather than from attacker-supplied lengths as in rows 14 and 18. The fix accordingly does not clamp the field; it threads the bitmap's length through a struct and bounds the write. That is why this is not a duplicate of the clamp rows.

spatial.oracle: fault at the labelled write probe
spatial.prediction: PREDICTED: faults. Every arm of this harness narrows a wmem allocation to its request via wm_narrow(), so a spatial crossing faults on ALL arms and this row does not discriminate the chunk port -- the corpus.json note states that for the corpus as a whole. NOT YET MEASURED for this case: it needs a Capstone domain build, which the four 2026-10-07 additions have not had.
spatial.note: ORACLE COMPLETED 2026-10-09, AFTER THE FIRST RUN, FROM THE SOURCE. The pre-registered text (kept in `prediction`) said only 'faults', naming neither probe nor cause, so the runner fell back to its defaults -- the READ probe and the temporal causes 24/25 -- and scored the first run FAIL although the domain faulted where the case is built to. The probe is fixed by case.c, which calls wm_write_probe at line 64; the cause by the access: a bounds violation on a store raises 7 (established by cases 16-17 on 2026-10-05). Neither was read off the result. MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/20261009-qemu-capstone-18-21/: cause 7 at pc=0x1019014e4, equal to the write probe address the boot published; runner exit 0 with controls 11 (temporal) and 13 (spatial) as recorded, negative control 12/12.
